# NOTES: THE NETHER MILLSTONE (Fred M. White, 1907, Little, Brown; Gutenberg #57312)
Single book, 60 chapters. Ask for detail by chapter.

## Front matter
- Frontispiece: "She came slowly down the steps and stood between the two men" (p.32). Other plates: p.15 "She playfully asked him not to be too long"; p.272 "Under the shade of a tree Mary laid down and closed her weary eyes"; p.397 "He had Mary's hand in his."
- Chapter titles: I "The Caste of Vere de Vere"; II Dashwood Hall; III Horace Mayfield; IV A Leaf from the Past; V The Sacrifice; VI A Cruel Misunderstanding; VII The Only Way; VIII Found!; IX The Parting Guest; X Skin Deep; XI The Dowager Lady Dashwood; XII Lady Dashwood Sees a Ghost; XIII Desecration!; XIV A Fierce Temptation; XV Not Quite Too Late; XVI The Unfinished Word; XVII Breathing Time; XVIII A Flaming Sword; XIX A Guardian Angel; XX Half Told; XXI Vincent Dashwood; XXII Who Did It?; XXIII The Silver Clue; XXIV A Fresh Calamity; XXV Pride or Prejudice; XXVI In Reckless Mood; XXVII A Warning; XXVIII Moral Force; XXIX Strategy; XXX The Heir of the House; XXXI Under Which Lord?; XXXII Must This Thing Be?; XXXIII A Rebel Against Fate; XXXIV Mistress Of Herself; XXXV A Friend in Need; XXXVI Connie Colam; XXXVII The Unexpected Happens; XXXVIII The Mystery Deepens; XXXIX Homeless; XL In Peril; XLI The Lesson of Adversity; XLII The Courage of Despair; XLIII Getting Nearer; XLIV The Dreary Way; XLV The Walls of Pride; XLVI The Head of the House; XLVII "How Long, How Long!"; XLVIII Face To Face!; XLIX A Bolt From the Blue; L Hard Put To It; LI Cold Comfort; LII The Spider's Web; LIII The Web Tightens; LIV "Eyes Clearer Grown----"; LV Not Dead; LVI Found!; LVII A Clean Breast Of It; LVIII "The King is Dead--"; LIX "Long Live the King!"; LX Open Confession.

## Cast
- **Mary Dashwood** (Mary Dashwood Mallory), 22, proud, chestnut hair, blue eyes; daughter of Sir George.
- **Ralph Darnley** = secretly **Sir Ralph Dashwood**, true heir; son of Ralph Dashwood (the younger, who left for America/California ~40 yrs ago) and his first wife **Maria Edgerton** (farmer's daughter, child-wife, died). Mother of Ralph later "Californian lady" (second marriage). Father described as "Mr. Darnley" who made silver-mining money in California. Brown eyes, tan, strong hands.
- **Sir George Dashwood** (formerly Mr. George Mallory-ish; was in Diplomatic Service, Paris); weak, vain, gambler, cowardly; cries; later "Mr. George Dashwood" after loss of title.
- **Horace Mayfield**: City financier, glass in left eye, hard mouth, cold, calculating; wants Mary; ruined Ralph's father and Ralph; holds judgment £5,193 17s 4d (also earlier £5,000 loan) against Sir George; sends three bailiffs ("Suit of Mayfield and Co.").
- **Slight**: old butler, pink/white, ~80+, loyal to Ralph's father; calls Ralph "Mr. Ralph"; witnessed deed.
- **Lady Dashwood** (dowager, Ralph's mother's rival; "Lady Dashwood", ~70, white hair); Ralph's mother was the wife she and old Sir Ralph drove out; she faked the death/hid; she sold jewels (~£30,000) to Vincent. Her son left home ~40 years ago; she fostered Mary's pride.
- **Patience Ray**: Mary's old nurse, demented, lucid at times; sets fires ("smoke the rats out").
- **Vincent Dashwood / Vincent Speed**: impostor, son of **Mrs. Speed** (Agnes Edgerton, Maria's sister, landlady at 16 Keppel Terrace, later No. 24 Hamerton Gardens). Blackmails Lady Dashwood; sets fire to Hall (matchbox "V.D." silver, paraffin, straw); steals papers; later ambushes Ralph.
- **Walters**: footman who saw figure; **Charles**: butler at dower house; **Kelly**: Mary's maid; **Gibbons**: station porter; **Seddon**: dinner servant; **Mr. Sayers**: fire official; **Inspector Drake** (Longtown head constable); **Dr. Newcome**; **Connie Colam** (general's daughter; illustrator for *The Wheezer*, *Razzle Dazzle*; friend); **Grace Cameron** (tubercular illustrator, supports widowed mother); **Mr. Morley** (family solicitor, Bedford Row); **Mr. Cotton**, **Mr. Newfell** (City men); **Mrs. Speed** lodging; **Mr. Scudamore** (editor).

## Plot in order
1. Ralph saves Mary's runaway horse at lych-gate (black horse; she was thrown toward church gate). Earlier Paris rescue. Mary refuses Ralph (son of Californian rancher). Mayfield ruined Ralph; Ralph came "to find something". Slight recognises Ralph ("Mr. Ralph"). Ralph arranged meeting at lodge-gates 10:30.
2. Ralph dines; Mayfield present. Sir George owes Mayfield £50,000. Mary: "dowager"; old Sir Ralph's quarrel; will not found; estate has life-interest. Mayfield pressed for Mary's hand. Sir George strikes Mayfield; collapses. Ralph kisses Mary.
3. Ralph finds will in panel by oak dower-chest in corridor (spring); Mary catches him ("Thief in the night"). Sir George discovers; Mary says "Hush".
4. Sir George finds will (dated 1877, 20-year clause) and deed cutting entail; Slight warns him to burn them. Mayfield's bailiffs come (three men: one in servants' hall, one upstairs, one in drawing-room; smoking pipe). Mayfield offers to clear debt if Mary marries him; Mary agrees by note; Slight refuses to deliver it, Walters takes it. Mary and Mayfield meet at midnight; Mayfield sends telegram; Lady Dashwood intervenes; Patience's nonsense.
5. Mayfield bribes bailiff to pose as electrical survey men; Lady Dashwood confronts Mayfield. Patience at Mary's room, speaks of Vincent, Mr. Vincent made Lady sell jewels.
6. Fire in hall: Mary trapped in room; Ralph rescues her with wet towels. Lady Dashwood meets Ralph; shows miniature; Vincent appears. Inspector finds paraffin, straw, matchbox (V.D.).
7. Papers stolen from Sir George's desk. Mayfield threatens to repossess; Mary decides to sacrifice. Ralph reveals Vincent is heir; Vincent produces marriage certificate (given by Ralph). Mayfield meets Vincent; blackmail demanded.
8. Mary refuses Vincent's offer; leaves for London third-class (Victoria). Connie Colam meets her, lodging at 16 Keppel Terrace. Mary's art attempts fail. Mrs. Speed flits; loss of luggage, jewels, purse; Mary sleeps on Embankment; traces Mrs. Speed to Hamerton Gardens; sees Vincent. Grace Cameron invited to dower house. Mary pawns diamond ring for £5.
9. Lady Dashwood tells Mary Vincent is impostor; learns Speed is Mrs. Speed's son; Ralph reveals himself to Lady Dashwood; Vincent's blackmail.
10. Vincent (as Sir Vincent) pawns; Speed plots with Mayfield to kill Ralph; Ralph struck down under verandah; Slight finds him under oak, takes him to dower house. Speed flees to Jersey by boat; drowns in storm. Mayfield vanishes (warrant).
11. Ralph and Mary reconcile; Mary's confession at bedside; Ralph reveals his identity (Sir Ralph) and his romantic plan; Mary agrees; plans to build retreat for artists; wedding under way at end. Last line: "THE END."
